video_title: Are The Lakers Breaking Up With LeBron James? 😳‼️ - Mason & Ireland

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Ramona Shelburne on the likelihood of Lakers free agents returning
quotes.excerpt: I think KCP is probably back. Rui I could see back, but depends on what other people throw.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Mason
text_blocks.text: Do you expect all five of those players to be on the Laker roster when this season starts?

text_blocks.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
text_blocks.text: I think KCP is probably back. That's one that he wants to stay, they want him to stay. Rui I could see back, but depends on what other people throw at him. Austin, I'm not as sure about. He was good for them, but he's older, injury prone, etc. There could be other younger guys they could get, so that's the one I'm not as sure about. I wouldn't say no, but I wouldn't say it's 100 percent.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Austin Reaves' potential free agency destinations
quotes.excerpt: The only question with Austin is are Brooklyn or Detroit or some of the others interested?

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Mason
text_blocks.text: Austin, I think he's coming back. The only question with Austin is, are Brooklyn or Detroit or some of the others interested?

text_blocks.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
text_blocks.text: I don't think Chicago. I don't think Detroit is the one where he would make a ton of sense. A lot of sense for them.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' ongoing contract discussions with the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: I know they're allowed to talk to your own free agents, so they've had some discussions already.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Mason
text_blocks.text: Do you have a sense for who those teams are, who are the real contenders if LeBron doesn't come back?

text_blocks.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
text_blocks.text: For me, it's pretty simple. It's either the Lakers, Cleveland, or Golden State. I would be really surprised if it's not one of those three. I think there's other teams that would make sense, but I don't see those as realistic. I know they're allowed to talk to your own free agents, so they've had some discussions already with LeBron and his agents about that, but I don't think we've even gotten to a numbers stage.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Why it is easier for LeBron James to leave the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: It's much easier for LeBron to break up with the Lakers than it is for the Lakers.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Mason
text_blocks.text: Do you think there's less of a chance LeBron comes back to the Lakers than he stays?

text_blocks.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
text_blocks.text: I think that it's much easier for LeBron to break up with the Lakers than it is for the Lakers to break up with LeBron. In other words, if another team comes at him with, 'Hey, we really want you, but all we can pay you is the mid-level,' that's not insulting to him because that's all they can. They're giving him the most they can give him. Whereas if the Lakers come to him and say, 'Okay, we'll give you 25 a year,' that's insulting to him because he makes 52 now.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.excerpt: When you look at restricted free agency there's two names, Jalen Duren and there's Walker Kessler.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Mason
text_blocks.text: What are they looking for in free agency?

text_blocks.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
text_blocks.text: When you look at restricted free agency there's two names, Jalen Duren and there's Walker Kessler. The Lakers would love to have either of them, but it's restricted free agency. So how do you get someone in restricted free agency? You either make an offer they can't refuse, which means you're probably overpaying for them. If you're doing Walker Kessler then maybe you're giving him 35, which is an overpay, but that's the only way you're going to get him.
